meta.about: Light and sky: both lighting rigs as the running game sets them, the sky and haze parameters, every lamp of the block, the lit signs and the windows that glow at night.
meta.readFrom: the running web game (window.__G, three.js r160), every module real

units.web: metres, seconds, radians; +Y up, north = -Z, east = +X (right-handed)
units.ue: centimetres, degrees; +Z up, X = east, Y = south (left-handed)

meta.conversion: ue (X, Y, Z) = web (x, z, y) * 100; ue yaw = atan2(web z, web x) of a direction = -rotationY of a prop, in degrees
meta.colours: `hex` is sRGB, `linear` is linear RGB (what an FLinearColor takes); radiance triples are scene-referred linear values where 1 is where bloom starts at night
meta.intensities: three.js r160 light units as the game sets them (the key and the ambient as directional / hemisphere intensities, a lamp as the intensity of the spot light it gets). They were tuned by eye against the exposure of the same rig: use them for the balance between lights, not as photometric values.

rigs.source: read from the scene after G.atmos.setTime(name): G.atmos.sun (the one shadow-casting directional light), the hemisphere light, scene.fog, G.render.look (the grade). The remaining fields of each rig are G.config.look.times[name].

fog.rule: opacity = 1 - exp(-(density * distance in metres)^2) (three.js FogExp2); past the play bounds the haze thickens (config.json look.fog.endReach / endClear) and is tinted warm toward the west, cool toward the east (look.fog.tintWest / tintEast by night, look.dayFogTint by day)

exposure.note: final exposure = exposure x multiplier (G.render.exposure), applied before the tone map; inside the shop it is multiplied by `interior.exposure`

bloom.note: threshold is scene-referred linear radiance before exposure

key.role: one steep warm key standing in for the street lights (the moon in the sky is `sky.night.moon`)

fog.rule: opacity = 1 - exp(-(density * distance in metres)^2) (three.js FogExp2); past the play bounds the haze thickens (config.json look.fog.endReach / endClear) and is tinted warm toward the west, cool toward the east (look.fog.tintWest / tintEast by night, look.dayFogTint by day)

exposure.note: final exposure = exposure x multiplier (G.render.exposure), applied before the tone map; inside the shop it is multiplied by `interior.exposure`

bloom.note: threshold is scene-referred linear radiance before exposure

sky.source: G.config.look (src/config/look.js): what the two sky domes are painted from. Radiance triples are linear.

sunDisc.note: the disc stands where the key light comes from

moonDisc.note: the moon is sky decoration; the night key light does not come from it

lamps.source: G.level.lamps: every light fixture of the block (the lamp hints of placed props included: `prop` is the index into props.json instances). aim: how the lamp shines when it holds one of the real lights, by the rule of src/atmos/lights.js (its own direction; a flood without one at the nearest reel; a sign or lit window out from the wall behind it and 35 degrees down; anything else straight down), checked here against the game's own spot lights for 56 of the 90 lamps. overDeck: the lamp hangs over a floor of the level (a platform, the mezzanine, the shed deck) at that height. By day only `work` lamps and dimmed `neon` lamps are lit (rigs.day.lampGain).

kinds.source: G.config.look.lamps: how each kind is drawn (ground pool, fixture glow, cone) and how strong its real light is

signLights.source: lamps: the `neon` entries of `lamps.list` (the light a sign throws on the sidewalk). signs: every lit sign quad (level.json signage; style 'neon' flickers, the others are lit boards), with its colours.

signs.sub: OPEN 24 HRS  ·  COLD CUTS  ·  COFFEE  ·  LOTTO

windowLights.source: lamps: the `window` entries of `lamps.list` (the light a lit shop throws out). glass: the level's lit panes (level.json glazing: storefronts, the station, transoms, the shop's skylights). facadeWindows: the lit windows of the painted facade grids (level.json facades). All of it glows at night only.

facade.source: src/mats/facade.js, read from the source text: a warm window takes one of `warm`; a tv window is a blue gradient
